name: Notifications
description: The platform's notification dispatcher. Resolves recipient preferences, per-category opt-outs and ONE quiet-hours model once, then fans out to channel providers contributed through `notification:channel`. Security/OTP traffic is exempt from every recipient-controlled gate via an urgency flag.
author: Kuray Karaaslan

failOpen.reason: A provider that throws knows nothing about any address; refusing every message would also stop password resets and security alerts.
failOpen.when: transactional and critical purposes only; marketing and other commercial purposes fail closed (consent, EXT-3)

extensionPoints.description: An ADDRESS-level gate: may we write to this address at all? Default export: { addressKind: 'EMAIL'|'SMS', isSuppressed(tenantId, address, { purpose }) } implementing SuppressionProvider. Separate from preferences because it answers a different question about a different subject — preferences need an account, suppression works on a guest address, a bounced mailbox or somebody who never had a login. Consulted BEFORE the CRITICAL exemption: urgency waives what the RECIPIENT chose, never what the ADDRESS is. A provider must FAIL CLOSED (an address it cannot evaluate is suppressed); the dispatcher fails OPEN on a provider error, because a broken provider knows nothing about anybody. Declared so `notification` never imports a CRM domain.

A delivery channel (mail, sms, push, inapp, or any open slug such as telegram). Default export: { channel, canDeliver?, deliver } implementing NotificationChannelProvider. A NEW channel (not one of the four core ids) must declare static `metadata` on its contribution so the policy can decide without loading it: { label, addressKind: 'EMAIL'|'SMS'|'ACCOUNT'|'EXTERNAL', respectsQuietHours: boolean } (respectsQuietHours is required; EXTERNAL channels resolve their own address in canDeliver and report no_address when unlinked). Its per-user toggle lives in user_preferences.channelPrefs[channel]. The dispatcher resolves policy BEFORE calling a provider, so a provider must not re-check preferences, category opt-outs or quiet hours — doing so applies the policy twice. Declared so `notification` never imports a channel module: the dispatcher stays installable with zero channels, and a tenant only gets the channels it has.
